pr.title: Promote the site through Vercel's API, and accept its revalidating cache header
pr.head: af96cd19a72860e11371acf071974b591d486877

summary: getmultipass.dev is a small Vercel site whose main job is to redirect /install.sh to the installer attached to a GitHub release. The Website workflow (.github/workflows/site.yml) deploys it on each merge to main. The workflow deploys without attaching the domain, then promotes the new deployment (points the domain at it). It checks the live redirects and rolls back (points the domain at the deployment it served before) when a check fails.

The workflow's first real run failed at the promote step with User not found. (404). The pinned Vercel CLI, vercel@65.14.0, looks up the token's user through GET /v2/user before it promotes or rolls back. The workflow's token is scoped to a Vercel team and has no user, so both commands fail with it.
This pull request makes three changes:

1. Direct API calls. The workflow calls Vercel's promote and rollback endpoints itself, through a new script, .github/scripts/vercel-api.sh, that keeps the token out of every process's arguments. It then polls the domain's alias until the domain serves the deployment it asked for.
  2. A cache rule that matches Vercel. Vercel sends public, max-age=0, must-revalidate on every redirect, whatever vercel.json asks for. So the live check, which demanded no-store, now accepts any header that makes every cache ask the site again.
  3. The plan catches up with rollout. The installer plan records what the first release and the first deploy found.

The workflow runs only on main with the token, so the new promote, alias wait, and rollback first run on the next Website deploy after the merge. tests/site.sh covers the script and the cache rule without any network access.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Deployment. One upload of site/ to Vercel, with an ID such as dpl_… and its own URL.
  • Alias. Vercel's record that the domain serves a given deployment. Its deploymentId says which.
  • Promote. Point the production domains at a deployment.
  • Roll back. Point them back at an earlier deployment.
  • Team-scoped token. A Vercel API token issued for a team rather than a person, so it has no user record.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: A Projector review of af96cd1 was clean, with no finding threads. It listed three suggestions: a curl time limit in vercel-api.sh, a format check on deployment IDs read from the API, and an early return for an empty value in the cache rule, which macOS's bash 3.2 otherwise aborts on.

groups.title: Promote and roll back through the API
groups.kicker: The workflow calls Vercel's REST API directly instead of the CLI's promote and rollback.
intro: The CLI still uploads the site with vercel deploy --prod --skip-domain, which works with a team token. Every step after the upload calls the API through vercel-api.sh <method> <path>. The script adds teamId to the path and prints the response body. It exits 0 for a 2xx answer, 4 for a 404, and 1 for any other answer, with the status and body on stderr.

1. Record. Read the domain's alias with GET /v4/aliases/getmultipass.dev and keep its deploymentId as the rollback target. A 404 means the domain was never promoted, so nothing is kept.
  2. Deploy. Upload with the CLI, which prints the new deployment's URL.
  3. Promote. Look the URL up with GET /v13/deployments/<host> to get its id, then call POST /v10/projects/<project>/promote/<id>.
  4. Wait. Read the alias every five seconds, 36 times, until it names the new ID. Promotion completes after the request returns.
  5. Check, and roll back on failure. Run the live redirect check. When the promote, the wait, or the check fails, call POST /v1/projects/<project>/rollback/<previous>, wait the same way for the alias to name the recorded deployment, and fail the job.

checks.text: Each endpoint, method, and field matches Vercel's published OpenAPI spec at openapi.vercel.sh: requestPromote and requestRollback are POST with no request body and a teamId query parameter, getDeployment accepts a hostname and returns id, and getAlias returns a nullable deploymentId. The review read the spec and called none of the endpoints.

files.note: New. The one place the workflow calls Vercel's API, with the token sent to curl on stdin.

checks.text: printf is a shell builtin, so the Authorization line exists only in the pipe to curl -H @-, never in a process's arguments. Nothing from a response is ever written to that stdin, so a response cannot add a header line.
curl runs with no --max-time, so the alias wait is bounded by its count of tries only while each request returns. The review suggested a time limit.

files.note: The promote and rollback steps call vercel-api.sh, and both wait for the alias. Permissions, the production environment, concurrency, triggers, and the pinned checkout action are unchanged.

checks.text: Steps run under GitHub's default bash -e, without pipefail, so a failed lookup is caught through the empty id that jq prints, not through the script's exit status.
The loop runs 36 times with five seconds between tries, about three minutes. It exits 0 as soon as the alias names the new deployment, and otherwise fails the step, which triggers the rollback.
The rollback step always fails the job. It names the deployment it rolled back to, or says that the alias never came back to it.

groups.title: Accept the cache header Vercel sends
groups.kicker: The live check accepts any Cache-Control value that makes every cache ask the site again.
intro: The live check makes sure no cache can serve an old redirect target. It used to require no-store. Vercel ignores vercel.json's headers on redirects and always sends public, max-age=0, must-revalidate, so every deploy would have failed its live check and rolled back.

That header is enough: max-age=0 makes a stored redirect stale at once, and must-revalidate forbids any cache from using a stale response without asking again (RFC 9111 § 5.2.2.2). The new rule accepts no-store, no-cache, or max-age=0 with must-revalidate. It refuses a positive s-maxage, which a shared cache would use in place of max-age. A new check-site.sh cache <value> mode applies the rule to one value, so the tests can reach it.

files.note: Adds cache_revalidates, the rule above, and the cache mode that runs it on one value.

checks.text: curl -sI https://getmultipass.dev/install.sh returns a 307 to the release URL with cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate, and check-site.sh live https://getmultipass.dev exits 0 at this head.

For an empty value the directives array is empty. macOS's bash 3.2 treats that array as unbound under set -u, so the script aborts there instead of returning 1. The answer is still a refusal, and the workflow runs on Linux's bash 5, where the rule runs normally.

groups.title: Offline tests for the script and the rule
groups.kicker: tests/site.sh checks vercel-api.sh against a fake curl and the cache rule against a table of values.
intro: CI runs tests/site.sh on every pull request. The new checks put a fake curl first on PATH. The fake writes its arguments and its stdin to files and answers with a chosen status. The checks then assert that the token is on stdin and not in the arguments, that teamId joins a path with or without a query, that a GET sends no body, and that a 404 and a 403 give their exit codes. A second table feeds header values to check-site.sh cache: Vercel's default and no-store must pass, and values that let a cache keep a redirect must fail.

checks.text: The run ends with site checks passed at this head and sends no request over the network.

groups.title: The installer plan records rollout
groups.kicker: The plan describes the API calls, the cache header, Vercel's wildcard DNS record, and what rollout verified.
intro: The installer plan, at status: in-progress, changes in four places. § 2.10's steps describe the API calls and say why the CLI cannot make them. § 2.9 explains Vercel's cache header and its fixed wildcard DNS record. The § 4 table changes the rows for the wildcard and the cache header. A new § 6.1 records the v0.1.0 release run, its attestation checks, the installs from the release, and the manual first promotion.

files.note: § 2.9, § 2.10 steps 5 to 8, the § 4 table, rollout step 4, and the new § 6.1.
